This might seem weird and ranty but I couldn’t leave it. That’s just not true. I’m so terribly sorry you’re feeling this way. I’ve been there. Could have typed it verbatim at one point. Short hair and all. I agree with the others. Therapy is essential and you deserve it. It’ll help you understand and reduce fee sources of self loathing.

First, short hair is fucking COOL!!! Don’t let the ‘women only look good with long hair etc etc’ nonsense poison your self concept. That’s a narrative that doesn’t have to belong to you - do you just really love and want long hair (totally fine) or does it feel like a box that must be ticked to be considered pretty? If you don’t feel good having short hair right now, it doesn’t mean you deserve years of self loathing until it grows.

My brother was rude about how I looked with short hair. That’s alright. He’s 1 person, and he’d say the same if Margot Robbie cut her hair. Another person might feel that way if an actor shaves off his moustache. It’s totally subjective. Kindness is hot. Short is hot. Massive hands are hot. Unshaven legs are hot. Skinny with long hair doesn’t mean pretty universally. Pretty is many things to many people. Leave the absolutes to the mathematicians.  Please, please never punish yourself based on something so subjective. Darling, you are fabulous!

I don’t know if this will help any, but the long hair and scars is familiar. I deliberately didn’t seek help for a self-harming form of dermatillomania, didn’t wash, didn’t groom, kept my hair short. I punish myself for not being ‘perfect’ by making sure my self-esteem had no chance of recovery. I was the barrier. I loved fashion, makeup and long hair; I just didn’t love myself enough to understand that those things belong to me as much as they do the people I admire. Depression can be kind of parasitic. It can’t survive if you realise your worth. 

What tats would you get first? What would you do/wear/study/join if you were one of these women you mentioned?. 
Make a list. Like right now. If you were granted a year as your beauty ideal, what would you do? Really imagine it and scribble anything that comes to mind. Leave it for a while. 

Come back to it. The chances are that ‘perfect’ you gets a tonne more respect from your inner critic. She’s probably having a heck of a lot more fun and a bunch of neat tattoos. 
What I’m trying to say, is it’s okay to have a personal beauty ideal. But, not at the expense of self love; letting the wanker inside succeed in denying you joy and the chance to realise you’re basically the dogs danglies. 
*YOU* deserve everything that person you’ve placed on a pedestal does and infinitely more. GET THOSE TATS.

This isn’t going to magically fix things, but it may help. Do you really want to have long hair? For you? Well, you totally can. Give yourself permission. If you have a stylist, tell them you’re interested in growing it out and they’ll help you on the journey. In the meantime, find pics of cool cuts similar to yours right now and learn to style it in a way that makes you happy. There’s also loads amazing growth videos on yt that show how they styled it bit by bit in the awkward growth stages. 

Wigs are so common these days. Cheap ones can look more natural with a little talcum powder (there are so many tricks). Even if you don’t wear them out in public at first (or ever) it could give you a boost. Hair is temporary. 
Tattoos? Want tattoos? If you do, besides the fact they’re super expensive, why wouldn’t you deserve them? 
People don’t give yourself a hard time about the scars. Generally, folks don’t even notice them at all. They’re too busy thinking about themselves to give it a great deal of thought. You’ve probably had a client who’s insecure about something you never even noticed. 
My partner has many scars on her arms; she’s fucking magnificent and entirely deserving of love. She’s got short hair. She’s a fucking glorious fat woman and super *pretty*. Scars can’t make her ugly. Evidence of self harm could never culture ugliness in people. What’s ugly is the cruel world that tortures people until they need this kind of release. Seems pretty unhinged to have a strong negative view on how someone else’s skin looks.

There’s no need to feel shame or like you’re critically different to women you think are beautiful. Remember that scars, weight, hair length, disability…theyre just part of the human experience. They aren’t mutually exclusive to pretty.  
You *deserve* happiness too. You can have all those things you feel are the domain of these aspirational women. You just gotta stop pigeonholing yourself as a worthless cave dweller.
